subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw add native backup exclude-pattern controls now, and which default exclusions and protected recovery paths should become part of the core CLI contract?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but the final behavior balances backup size, sensitive-file avoidance, and restorable archives, which is a maintainer product/security choice.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, and proof before landing or narrowing it.

options.title: Narrow to explicit excludes first
options.body: Accept `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` while deferring smart defaults until restore completeness and security expectations are clearer.

options.title: Decline native excludes for now
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document the current scope, and point optional backup strategies to plugin or ClawHub paths after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, and proof before landing or narrowing it.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original backup CLI and have adjacent refactor history in the backup implementation, making them the strongest routing candidate for the core CLI contract decision.
